title: Merge k Sorted Lists
statement:
You are given an array of `k` linked lists, each sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked lists into one sorted linked list and return it.

Build a real `ListNode` chain for each input list, then merge all `k` chains using a min-heap (or by repeatedly merging pairs, divide-and-conquer style) keyed on node value. Return the merged chain as a single sorted array.
constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10^4

editorial.approach: Merging two sorted lists at a time (as in Merge Two Sorted Lists) and repeating that k-1 times is O(k*n) overall. A faster approach: merge lists in pairs, divide-and-conquer style — merge list 0 with 1, list 2 with 3, etc., then repeat on the resulting half-sized set of lists, until only one list remains. This does O(log k) merge 'rounds', each doing O(n) total work across all lists, giving O(n log k) overall. A min-heap keyed on the front node's value works too, popping the smallest and pushing its successor.
editorial.complexity: O(n log k) time / O(k) space, where n is the total number of nodes
